struck: Entitlement is restored after you sell and pay off a VA loan.
use: After you sell the home and pay off the VA loan, you can ask the VA to restore your entitlement.

struck: A qualified surviving spouse keeps it, and can move it to a later home.
use: A surviving spouse who has not remarried and lives in the home keeps it, and can move it to a later home.

struck: A newly rated veteran can claim the exemption for the whole year the disability began.
use: A newly rated veteran can claim the exemption for the whole year the disability began, if they owned the home that year; if they bought it later, from the year they bought it.

struck: At 65 the Homestead Exemption takes the first $50,000 of the home's value off the bill.
use: At 65, with a year in South Carolina, the Homestead Exemption takes the first $50,000 of your home's value off the bill; for 2026 only, owners who already qualified in 2025 get $75,000.

struck: The nearest VA medical center with a hospital is the Ralph H. Johnson VA Medical Center in Charleston.

struck: Your entitlement is the amount the VA agrees to pay your lender if you do not repay the loan. Your COE shows it.
use: Your entitlement is the most the VA will pay your lender if you do not repay the loan. Your COE shows your basic entitlement. The rest, for a larger loan, is worked out from the loan amount and is not on the COE.

pattern: \bthe VA works out what you have left\b
